results.title: Back Up and Restore in Termux
results.text:
First, stop the desktop and `exit` the distro, so no files change while it's saved. Then, in Termux:

```bash copy
andronix backup debian --to storage
```

This writes `andronix-debian-.tar.gz` to the **Andronix/backups** folder in your phone's storage. It's safe there even if you uninstall Termux, and you can see it in your file manager. If Termux doesn't have storage access yet, Android asks you for it.

Without `--to storage`, the backup goes to Termux's home folder instead. That folder is deleted if you uninstall Termux or clear its data. You can also give your own file name: `andronix backup debian ~/my-debian.tar.gz`.

results.title: Coming from Termux
results.text:
In Termux (type `exit` first if the distro is running), run:

```bash copy
andronix backup debian --to storage
```

Replace `debian` with your distro. Allow Termux to use your files when Android asks. The backup goes to **Internal storage › Andronix › backups**, with a name like `andronix-debian-20261005-1430.tar.gz`.

results.title: The andronix Command
results.text:
```bash
andronix backup <distro> [file] [--to storage]
andronix restore [file]
```

- `backup` saves the whole distro to one file: with `--to storage`, in `Andronix/backups` in your phone's storage; otherwise in Termux's home folder, or at the file name you give.
- `restore` brings a backup back. Without a file name, it lists the backups it finds and lets you pick one.

See [Back up and restore](/use/backups).

results.title: The Install Fails or Stops
results.text:
The installer checks your free space before it starts, and warns you if it looks too low. Roughly how much a distro takes once installed:

| Install | Space used |
|---|---|
| Command line only | 250 to 400 MB |
| XFCE or LXQt desktop | 0.8 to 1.6 GB |
| MATE desktop | 1.5 to 1.9 GB |
| KDE Plasma desktop | about 2.5 GB |

Leave some extra room for the download while it unpacks. If you're short on space, free some up, pick a smaller desktop, or use the command line only. Use `andronix list` to see what's installed, and [remove](/install/uninstall) distros you don't use.

Distros can only be installed on your phone's internal storage, not on an SD card. See [Limitations](/reference/limitations#hardware-limitations).

results.title: Phone Storage
results.text:
In Termux (not inside the distro), run:

```bash copy
termux-setup-storage
```

Termux will now ask for Storage permission. **Allow the Storage permission**.

results.title: Phone Storage
results.text:
To share another Termux folder with the distro, add a line to a file in `~/-binds/` in Termux, the same way as with the pre-2.0 installer. For example, to make Termux's `~/projects` folder appear at `/projects` in Debian:

```bash copy
mkdir -p ~/debian-binds
echo 'command+=" -b /data/data/com.termux/files/home/projects:/projects"' > ~/debian-binds/projects.sh
```

Restart the distro for the change to take effect.

Installed before Andronix 2.0? See [Storage on an old install](/pre-2.0/old-install-guides#storage-on-an-old-install).

```bash
andronix cache purge --all --force
```

Then run the install again.
